channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: South Korean Won: Reform-driven support for won – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Dr. Henry Hao and Moses Lim highlight that the South Korean government has unveiled a major South Korean Won (KRW) internationalisation roadmap, including unlimited KRW transactions with foreign institutions from January 2027 and broader access to onshore markets.

item.title: British Pound: Fiscal shield tests gilt and FX credibility – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu argues that Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s removal of Value Added Tax (VAT) on household electricity is a test of the United Kingdom’s (UK) fiscal protection strategy.

item.title: WTI Crude Oil advances on US-Iran supply disruption fears as traders await API report
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) trades around $84.40 at the time of writing on Tuesday, up 2.6% on the day, as concerns over global Oil supplies continue to support prices despite hopes for a diplomatic de-escalation in the Middle East.

item.title: British Pound drops as geopolitical risk premium revives USD
item.description: The Pound Sterling loses some ground against the US Dollar, down by 0.48%, as risk appetite in the foreign exchange markets deteriorates, with the Greenback reclaiming key technical levels in the US Dollar Index (DXY) amid the escalation of the US-Iran conflict.

item.title: USD/CHF Price Forecast: Buyers hold the upper hand above 0.8000
item.description: USD/CHF edges higher as escalating tensions in the Middle East support the US Dollar (USD), with buyers eyeing a breakout above the 0.8150 resistance level that has capped gains since July 2025. At the time of writing, the pair trades around 0.8123, up 0.27% on the day.

item.title: US President Trump: “We’re not finished at all with Iran”
item.description: United States (US) President Donald Trump said during a press conference at the White House on Tuesday that Washington could intensify its military campaign against Iran, including possible strikes on the underground Pickaxe Mountain site.

item.title: Dow Jones Industrial Average rebounds on earnings as Trump trades one war for another
item.description: The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) climbs around 340 points, or 0.7%, on Tuesday, snapping a three-day slide that has pulled the index away from the early July record just above 53,300.

item.title: India: Weather-driven inflation risks – Standard Chartered
item.description: Standard Chartered Bank economist Saurav Anand highlights rising inflation risks for India as deficient monsoon rains and persistent El Niño threaten food output. The report notes sowing is down and reservoir levels are low, with pulses, vegetables, sugar and oilseeds most exposed.

item.title: USD/JPY climbs above 163.00 for the first time since 1986
item.description: USD/JPY trades higher near 163.00 on Tuesday after briefly reaching 163.04, marking its first move above the 163.00 level since December 1986. The US Dollar (USD) remains supported by safe-haven demand as investors assess renewed Middle East tensions and rising Oil prices.

item.title: Australian Dollar retreats from a monthly high
item.description: AUD/USD trades lower near the 0.7010 area on Tuesday, although the pair has retreated from its four-week high. The Australian Dollar (AUD) remains above the psychological 0.7000 level as softer United States (US) economic data limits demand for the US Dollar (USD).

item.title: Euro slips as war boosts US Dollar despite upbeat ZEW surveys
item.description: EUR/USD edges lower on Tuesday as the US Dollar (USD) strengthens amid continued strikes between the US and Iran. At the time of writing, the pair trades around 1.1405, hovering near one-week lows.

item.title: British Pound: Fiscal flexibility weighs on Pound – ING
item.description: ING’s Francesco Pesole notes that Gilts and the Pound saw turbulence as new UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham signalled flexibility on fiscal rules and appointed John Healey as Chancellor.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD surges as Middle East hostilities boost safe-haven demand
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) rallies to around $58.85 on Tuesday at the time of writing, up 4.31% on the day. The white metal is supported by strong safe-haven demand as investors continue to monitor escalating tensions between the United States (US) and Iran.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Tariff shock weighs as Trump raises duties – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu explains that new 50% U.S. tariffs on selected Canadian goods are a direct trade shock, with Washington citing unfair treatment of US exports and ruling out United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA) exemptions.

item.title: Euro: Range-bound against US Dollar ahead of ECB – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret highlight the Euro (EUR) trading quietly against the US Dollar (USD) in a tight low-1.14 range, with limited reaction to stronger ZEW sentiment data. Short-term rates have stabilized after a hawkish repricing, supporting EUR via yield spreads.

item.title: British Pound: Fiscal uncertainty caps upside against US Dollar – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad highlights that the sell-off in gilts and British Pound (GBP) has stabilized after Prime Minister Andy Burnham appointed John Healey as Chancellor and pledged to stick to fiscal rules.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Mean reversion faces tariff headwinds – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale strategists note that softer June inflation in Canada has stalled the Canadian Dollar’s (CAD) rebound from 1.4250 toward 1.40 against the US Dollar (USD). Failure to reclaim the 50-day moving average around 1.3991 and new US tariffs on Canadian goods complicate the mean-reversion.

item.title: US Dollar: Complacency risk supports Dollar – ING
item.description: ING strategists Francesco Pesole, Frantisek Taborsky and Chris Turner note that the Dollar is drawing broad-based support as markets slowly react to escalating tensions in the Gulf.

item.title: Canadian Dollar retreats as new US tariff threat, softer inflation weigh
item.description: USD/CAD trades on the front foot as tensions in the Middle East keep the US Dollar (USD) firmly bid, while the Canadian Dollar also faces pressure from renewed trade frictions with the United States.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Japan’s fiscal pivot and GPIF flows reshape rates – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu highlights Japan’s new fiscal guidelines under Prime Minister Takaichi, which prioritize proactive spending and long-term investment over near-term consolidation.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar dips despite hotter inflation as firm US Dollar caps gains
item.description: NZD/USD trades around 0.5835 on Tuesday at the time of writing, down a modest 0.07% on the day despite support for the New Zealand Dollar (NZD) from stronger-than-expected inflation data.

item.title: British Pound: Funding concerns weigh on Sterling – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank's Senior FX Strategist Jane Foley discusses United Kingdom (UK) markets’ reaction to PM Burnham’s new cabinet and fiscal plans, noting 10-year gilt yields above 5% and British Pound (GBP) weakness in G10.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Tariff risks cap gains against US Dollar – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret note the Canadian Dollar (CAD) has recovered overnight losses versus the US Dollar (USD) after news that President Trump may impose new tariffs on Canadian exports.

item.title: Gold climbs as buyers defend $4,000, hawkish Fed expectations limit upside
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) edges higher on Tuesday as buying interest around the $4,000 psychological level supports prices, while traders assess developments in the Middle East and their potential economic fallout. At the time of writing, XAU/USD trades around $4,060, up 1.30% on the day.

item.title: Euro gains against British Pound as Burnham’s fiscal stance weighs
item.description: EUR/GBP gains on Tuesday as doubts over the UK’s fiscal outlook weigh on the British Pound (GBP) following Andy Burnham’s appointment as Prime Minister. At the time of writing, the cross trades around 0.8527.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar: CPI supports further RBNZ hikes – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad reports NZD/USD has rallied toward a seven-week high after New Zealand Q2 Consumer Price Index (CPI) surprised slightly on the upside versus consensus but came in just below the Reserve Bank of New Zealand's (RBNZ) projection.

item.title: Aluminium: Output declines on regional disruptions – ING
item.description: ING’s Warren Patterson and Ewa Manthey highlight a softening Aluminium supply picture. Global primary output fell in June on both monthly and yearly bases, even as first-half production stayed broadly stable.

item.title: US ADP Employment Change 4-week average drops to 16.5K
item.description: Private-sector hiring in the US has further cooled in early July. According to the NER Pulse, the weekly companion to the ADP National Employment Report, companies added an average of 16.5K jobs per week in the four weeks ending July 4.

item.title: British Pound: Fiscal policy uncertainty and Sterling reaction – MUFG
item.description: Lee Hardman at MUFG highlights that the Pound has modestly recovered after losses following Andy Burnham’s appointment as UK Prime Minister, while long-dated gilts remain under pressure.

item.title: Turkish Lira: Rising inflation expectations pressure TRY – Commerzbank
item.description: Tatha Ghose at Commerzbank highlights that Turkey’s market-based inflation expectations for 2026 and 12 months ahead have risen again, undermining confidence in disinflation.
